answer: Witness-anchored ledger divergence. Each identity must co-sign a shared ledger with its counterparties, and any clone appearing under an unused key triggers a mirror comparison across those ledgers. A duplicated agent leaves a distinct plume of conflicting entries that honest peers flag automatically. Because every identity also anchors a willow-shaped chain of prior interactions, cloning forces the attacker to reconstruct that entire history per copy, paying full compute and coordination cost each time.
